name: CR-Int-15-partialfrac-4.b
questiontext:
By expressing the integrand as the sum of its partial fractions, find the following definite integral:
\[ \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
In order to calculate \[\int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] we need to express \[{{CT:2}}\] as the sum of its partial fractions <hint>alg_partial_fractions</hint>.

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 {{CT:2}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}{{CT:8}}
 \end{array}\]

Omitting details we have \[{{CT:2}} = {{CT:9}},\]
hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:9}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:3}} + {{CT:11}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:12}} + {{CT:13}} +c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}} +c
 \end{array}\]

We need \[\int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}\] so, recall that if \[\int f(x) dx = F(x)\] then \[\int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b).\]

Thus, define \[F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:15}}\]

Then,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \int^{{CT:0}}_{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  F({{CT:0}}) - F({{CT:1}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:16}} - \left[{{CT:17}}\right] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:18}}
 \end{array}\]
